newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek investors hit by Albanian crisis seek aid.
newsitem.headline: Greek investors hit by Albanian crisis seek aid.

text.p: Greek investors in Albania asked their government to help them survive the upheaval in their Balkan neighbour.

"The need to support Greek business leaders in Albania is of primary importance," the Association of Northern Greek Exporters said in a statement issued during a Balkan economic conference in this northern Greek city.
Violence erupted in January in Europe's poorest country after the collapse of pyramid investment schemes that left thousands destitute.

"The damages, especially in southern Albania, are huge and can only be calculated accurately after the situation there normalises," the association said. "Immediate measures by the Greek state are vital."

Greek investment in Albania is second only to Italy's. Greek business leaders have defied the difficulties of emerging Balkan economies and boosted Greek exports to the Balkans by 239 percent from 1989 and 1995, the association said.

"We have posted guards at our worksites," Constantine Sarandopoulos, president of the K.I.Sarandopoulos construction firm, told Reuters. "Our construction site near Elbasan, where we are building a road and a bridge, was raided and destroyed."
The head of one of Greece's biggest construction firms with a long history of road-building in Albania, Sarandopoulos said that firms not only faced damage to materials but staffing problems as well.
"Material damages can be repaired. But the damage to the manpower is worse; people got scared and have left," he said.

Sarandopoulos urged the West to send an international police force to restore order in Albania and to come up with the cash to reimburse people who lost their life's savings in the fraudulent investment schemes.
"We need to give the money to help people survive financially," he said.

Greek National Economy Minister Yannos Papandoniou told the two-day conference that Athens was ready to extend Albania a loan on favourable terms as soon as the political situation in Albania normalises.

"Greece is prepared to guarantee a loan...with favourable terms to partly compensate those who lost their savings in the bankrupt pyramid schemes as well as the recovery and modernisation of the Albanian credit system," he said.
